accepted.name: THE HARBINGER / Xianquzhe
accepted.access: Creator-distributed beta; earlier betas explicitly free
accepted.note: The creator announces v0.0.4 and directs users through their pinned Bilibili/Afdian distribution post. An exact current download file, price and Minecraft/loader pair were not independently established. Earlier free-beta wording is not silently extended into a current price guarantee.
accepted.reason: Heavy science-fiction firearms, an exoskeleton autocannon and experimental railgun presentation distinguish this creator-authored pack from another conventional rifle collection. The discontinued ESSENCE predecessor is not counted again as a separate current pack.

accepted.name: Sentinel Technology / STF
accepted.access: Creator-hosted engineering test; current price unconfirmed
accepted.note: The creator identifies this as an engineering-test edition, not a final stable release. Transforming gun showcases and the public Afdian destination are verified, but the current paid/free terms and exact downloadable version are not. Arcana appears in the creator's stated requirements/credits.
accepted.reason: Transforming Destiny-inspired firearms and animated Dingo/Cloudstrike-style weapons offer unusually useful shape-change and first-person handling references. This is a separately named pack by an existing ecosystem creator, not a duplicate of EMX.

accepted.name: Team Fortress 2's Gun / TFG
accepted.note: The author-maintained project page describes a free Java 1.20.1 TaCZ pack; the creator announces v2.1.5. No exact current file/loader pair was independently retrieved. Planned weapons and melee/utility equipment are not counted as additional released firearms.
accepted.reason: A coherent Team Fortress 2-inspired firearm roster with distinctive silhouettes and medigun-style presentation, rather than recolored default TaCZ guns. Public author and programmer credits are retained.

accepted.name: Extreme Armaments / Ningmeng Craft
accepted.originalName: 极限武装 / 宁萌工艺
accepted.access: Public creator releases; current MPX file location unconfirmed
accepted.note: The same creator publishes MPX and earlier MK14 releases under this evolving project lineage. They are grouped conservatively, not claimed to be one combined current ZIP. The linked MK14 share comes from the original announcement; the MPX post redirects to a newer video. The later AX50 is explicitly unfinished and is not counted as released.
accepted.reason: An overlooked creator lineage with a released MPX and earlier MK14, useful for studying compact weapon proportions and handling. The evidence separates actual release announcements from the creator's later unfinished AX50 preview.

accepted.name: Dragon Technology
accepted.note: The original 2025 creator announcement supplies the public download and describes Mechanical Dragon plus the redesigned Star Dragon's Wish. A later similarly named GitHub tag has no uploaded release assets and is not presented as a newly released playable binary. The exact current Minecraft/loader pairing remains unconfirmed.
accepted.reason: Original dragon-themed science-fiction firearms, including Mechanical Dragon and Star Dragon's Wish. The unusual mechanical creature silhouette is particularly relevant to original AoA energy-weapon concepts.

accepted.name: TRW Low Maintenance Rifle / TaCZ LMR
accepted.note: The creator supplies lmr-1.0.0.zip and states TaCZ 1.1.4 or newer. The repository contains standard and tactical gun indexes. This is a small 2025 historical-design reference; no exact Minecraft/loader compatibility or native runtime quality is inferred.
accepted.reason: A focused, easily missed historical firearm pack with standard and tactical TRW Low Maintenance Rifle variants. Its released ZIP and actual TaCZ gun-index metadata distinguish it from a source template or attachment utility.

accepted.name: XColorful's TaCZ-PUBG
accepted.access: Public source snapshot; no packaged release verified
accepted.note: The creator explicitly stopped updating this project. Its public gunpack folder has a TaCZ namespace manifest and Beryl M762, Groza and SLR gun indexes, but no tagged playable release. This is labeled a legacy source reference, not a current plug-and-play recommendation. The separate creator's HK416/AUG packs are not merged by game title.
accepted.reason: An original creator's published PUBG-inspired gunpack source with Beryl M762, Groza and SLR. Useful as a clearly labeled legacy modeling reference, not promoted into the polished-current shortlist.

gh-1408153987.reason: A named ZIP exists, but no independently established firearm roster or creator preview. Not promoted merely from an archive name.

gh-1175195421.reason: Mechanics project advertises a WarBorn pack, but the inspected source tree has no gunpack manifest or released firearm bundle. Supporting mechanics are not counted as guns.

gh-1316797585.reason: TaCZ runtime fork with default assets and no separately released, qualified Strinova gunpack.

gh-1364139189.reason: The described firearm content belongs to a later roadmap, not a verified released gunpack.

gh-1423912084.reason: Curios/charm integration consumes existing TaCZ weapons rather than adding a gun roster.

gh-1414291131.reason: Browser armory/reference content, not the source of an independently authored gunpack.

bilibili-BV1Cm1eB7EQg.reason: A predecessor weapon subset has a public share, but separate durable family identity is not established. Not counted again beside Harbinger.

bilibili-BV19EEm6gE1q.reason: The same Extreme Armaments creator labels AX50 unfinished. The MPX/MK14 release lineage alone is counted.

metricPolicy: Only exact project/file popularity belongs in ranking fields. Bilibili views, video likes, author followers and GitHub stars are not converted into gunpack downloads, favorites or ratings. Unknown fields remain null.
qualityPolicy: Four new editorial study selections, two focused legacy/source references and one creator release lineage. Selection does not claim native Minecraft compatibility, measured performance or full video playback review.
